delivery.intro: We never publish a price up front — because the price depends on your address, your quantity, and that day's market rate. This page explains the three things in plain words, so you know why the rate changes before you call.
delivery.factor1Body: How far your site is from Singair, the road condition, and whether the truck can physically get in — these decide the freight part of the rate.
delivery.factor2Body: How many thousand bricks, how many CFT of sand, how many bags of cement, how many tons of rebar. Larger quantities usually bring the unit rate down.
delivery.factor3Body: The morning rate at the kiln and the crusher — that's what we share with you. Last week's rate and today's rate won't be the same.
delivery.exampleBody: A small load down a nearby lane and a full truck to a site in Savar will be priced differently — because one needs a small truck down a narrow road, the other needs a big truck on a good road but covering more distance. Tell us the address and quantity and we'll tell you the rate on the call.

delivery.tipsTitle: When the load arrives — what to check
delivery.tipsSubtitle: These are general tips from experience. We don't guarantee a specific count or weight as a company, but a quick check on your end keeps everything honest.
delivery.tipsBricksBody: If you're buying per 1,000 pieces, count as the bricks come off the truck. Pieces per row × rows — multiply and verify.
delivery.tipsSandBody: Measure the truck body's length × width × height to work out the CFT. Loose sand looks like less — stack it on flat ground and re-measure if you can.
delivery.tipsCementBody: Check each bag's seal. Cut or damp bags should be replaced — that's on us, just point it out on delivery.
delivery.tipsRebarBody: Match the bundle weight or piece count. Confirm the sizes (8, 10, 12 mm, etc.) and take a receipt.
